## How to use the Unix Timestamp Converter

Start by typing or pasting your unix timestamp (seconds). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Type or paste your unix timestamp (seconds).
2. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
3. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Unix seconds count from 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC. JavaScript Date uses milliseconds.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Unix Timestamp Converter](/unix-timestamp-converter) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 1767225600 represents 1 January 2026 00:00:00 UTC. Try the same figures in the [Unix Timestamp Converter](/unix-timestamp-converter) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Unix timestamp (seconds): 1767225600), the [Unix Timestamp Converter](/unix-timestamp-converter) returns UTC date and time: 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z, Local date and time: 1/1/2026, 12:00:00 AM, Milliseconds timestamp: 1,767,225,600,000. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly.
